title_guess: GDP at factor cost vs GDP at market price, built from one laptop sold through one shop, with tax added and a 3-year table
recurring_cast: laptop icon in a blue box with '10K ₹'
shopkeeper at a counter in a pink box with '+5K ₹' (shop)
purple customer figure with the price paid (15K, later struck to 18K)
india_map labelled GDP (beside or under the flow)
red round TAX badges on the two flow arrows (tax_badge)
black frame around the laptop-shop-customer flow
GDP split into two branches, Factor Cost and Market Price
multicoloured question marks (puzzle and comment prompts)
year table 2020-2022 with factor cost and market price columns
running_examples: one laptop made for Rs 10,000 (factor cost) and sold by a shop that adds Rs 5,000 of service, customer pays 15,000; GDP at factor cost 15,000
20% tax on each transaction: 2,000 on the laptop, 1,000 on the service, customer pays 18,000; GDP at market price 18,000 (shopkeeper's cost 12,000 is spoken only)
factory month: rent 20K + wages 20K + interest 20K + profit 40K = 100K; 10 laptops, so 10K per laptop
three years: factor cost 15K, 15K, 15K; market price 18K, 20K, 25K as indirect taxes rise

best_moments.why: a blue band rises from the laptop into the GOODS box with a tick, later a pink band rises from the shopkeeper into the SERVICES box with a tick and '+5K': each part of one sale is sorted into its GDP box
red TAX badges drop onto both arrows of the sale, '2K' and '1K' appear at each badge, and the customer's 15K is struck and rewritten 18K: tax added at each step lands on the final price
the GDP label grows two branches that first end in '15K' and '18K' and are then named Factor Cost and Market Price: the two terms arrive as names for two numbers the learner already has

a two-column table pairs each factor with its payment (entrepreneur-profit, land-rent, labour-wages, capital-interest); amounts 40K, 20K, 20K, 20K draw on arrows and sum to 100K, and 'number of laptops = 10' turns it into 10K per laptop
a 3-year table keeps factor cost at 15K every year while the market price column climbs 18K, 20K, 25K and an up-arrow over 'indirect taxes' grows taller: same production, bigger GDP at market price
a hand reaching out from the question card points at 'Factor Cost', which lights up green as the answer

weak_moments.why: the opening re-shows the previous video's whole canvas, with a four-line rule panel in small text and a 1-6 step counter, before the new idea; dense and only half explained
about 12 s of speech (14.7-26.9 s) is missing from the transcript while the laptop is sorted into GOODS; one recognised word is stretched over the gap

factors of production are a text list; 'capital' branches to raw material, machines, marketing and transport, which mixes factor payments with purchased inputs; the bank icon carries a real bank's name
the shop's factor cost is said to include electricity and machine maintenance, which are intermediate costs rather than factor incomes; doubtful, check before reuse
subsidies are in the market price formula but never get a number in the example
the pink label says 'price of 1 laptop 10K' while the speech calls it the cost of making one laptop (factor cost); in a video about cost vs price the label uses the wrong word
the green highlight jumps to Market Price while the voice is still saying India used to calculate GDP at factor cost

segments.teaches: recall of last video's puzzle: if a shopkeeper buys a 10,000 laptop and sells it to a customer for 15,000, what happens to GDP?

elements.what: left panel: four GDP rules from the previous video (Indian and foreign companies producing in India, goods exchanged for money, final goods)
yellow box with two cards: aggregate of all goods / all services produced in a financial year
India map labelled GDP, arrow from the yellow box
laptop '10K ₹' → shopkeeper at a counter → customer '15K ₹' in a blue band
cluster of coloured question marks under the GDP map
1-6 step counter at bottom left, step 6 raised (previous video's points)

segments.notes: 6 change events in 14 s (~every 2 s), each landing on the spoken word (shopkeeper, 10,000, 15,000, asar). Reuses the last frame of the previous video as a recall.
segments.idea: the puzzle: how does one laptop sale with a markup count in GDP?
segments.shown_as: the previous video's GDP canvas is back (rule panel, goods and services boxes, India map); under it a shopkeeper at a counter pops in, a laptop with 10K slides in with an arrow to him, a customer appears with 15K, and a cluster of question marks pops under the GDP map as the narrator asks the effect on GDP
segments.example: laptop bought at 10,000, sold to a customer at 15,000

segments.teaches: the laptop is a good worth 10,000 and the shopkeeper's 5,000 markup is a service; if this is the only laptop made in India in a year, GDP is 15,000

elements.what: blue band from the laptop up into the GOODS card, green tick on the arrow, '10K' above the card
pink band from the shopkeeper up into the SERVICES card, tick, '+5K ₹' under the shopkeeper, '5K' above the card

segments.notes: 3 change events in 31 s. The rule panel and counter drop away. Transcript gap 14.7-26.9 s (the shopkeeper's costs: rent, bills). GDP = 15,000 is spoken at 52-56 s, after this layout.
segments.idea: a sale splits into a good (the laptop) and a service (the shop's markup), and both count in GDP
segments.shown_as: the view closes on the goods and services boxes and the sale; a blue band rises from the laptop into the GOODS card with a green tick and '10K' over it; then a pink band rises from the shopkeeper into the SERVICES card with a tick, '+5K' under the shopkeeper and '5K' over the card

segments.teaches: GDP = 15,000 with no tax; but every transaction has tax: at 20%, 2,000 on the laptop (the shop's cost becomes 12,000) and 1,000 on the 5,000 service; all indirect taxes pass to the customer, who pays 18,000

elements.what: black frame round laptop (blue, 10K) → shopkeeper (pink, +5K) → customer (15K)
India map under the frame, 'GDP 15K' below it
red round TAX badges on both arrows
'2K ₹' under the first badge, '1K ₹' above the second
customer's 15K struck in red, 18K written below

segments.notes: Only 2 detected events in 60 s, but the tax amounts and the strike appear on their spoken numbers (kf 79.7, 89.7, 109.7). The shop's 12,000 cost is spoken (79-84 s) but not shown. The 20% rate is spoken, never shown.
segments.idea: taxes on each step push the customer's price above the value produced
segments.shown_as: the sale is redrawn in a black frame over an India map with 'GDP 15K'; red TAX badges drop onto both arrows, '2K' writes under the first and '1K' above the second, and the customer's 15K is struck through in red and rewritten 18K
segments.example: 20% tax: 2,000 on 10,000 and 1,000 on 5,000; customer pays 18,000 instead of 15,000

segments.teaches: so is GDP 15,000 or 18,000? The answer needs two concepts: GDP can be measured at factor cost and at market price

elements.what: GDP label grows two coloured branches ending in '15K' and '18K'
branch ends renamed 'Factor Cost' (red) and 'Market Price' (green)

segments.notes: 3 change events in 23 s, each on its word (15,000 or 18,000; factor cost; market price).
segments.idea: the same GDP has two values, one without taxes (factor cost) and one with them (market price)
segments.shown_as: under the framed sale the GDP label splits into two branches that end in '15K' and '18K' as the question is asked; the two ends are then relabelled Factor Cost and Market Price as the terms are named

segments.teaches: factor cost is the cost of producing a good or service; producing needs an entrepreneur, land, labour and capital; capital buys raw material, machines, marketing and transport, and can be borrowed from a bank on interest

elements.what: laptop '10K ₹' in a framed blue box at top left
'Factor Cost' with the line 'cost of producing this good/service'
list: entrepreneur, land, labour, capital
capital branches to raw material, machines, marketing, transportation in a blue panel labelled MONEY
bank building icon with a real bank's name and 'funds for startups', arrow to MONEY

segments.notes: 5 change events in 36 s. Capital's branches mix purchased inputs (raw material, transport) with the factor itself. Real bank brand on the icon (BIE will not use it).
segments.idea: making anything needs four factors: entrepreneur, land, labour, capital (money, often borrowed)
segments.shown_as: the canvas clears to the laptop in a framed box with 'Factor Cost' and a one-line definition under it; a four-item list (entrepreneur, land, labour, capital) writes on; arrows fan out from capital to raw material, machines, marketing and transport inside a blue panel tagged MONEY, and a bank icon pops in with an arrow feeding MONEY

segments.teaches: each factor earns a payment: profit, rent, wages and salaries, interest; a month of rent 20K, wages 20K, interest 20K and a target profit 40K costs 1 lakh; 10 laptops a month means 10,000 per laptop, and that is its factor cost

elements.what: yellow column of factors paired with a blue column of payments (profit, rent, wages and salaries, interest); laptop box moves to top right
arrows from each payment to its amount: 20K, 20K, 20K, 40K
'number of laptops produced = 10' at top
pink 'price of 1 laptop 10K ₹' over the laptop box

segments.notes: 4 detected events in 60 s; the amounts write on with their spoken numbers (kf 189.7-229.7). The label says 'price' where the narration says cost of making.
segments.idea: factor cost per unit = all factor payments for a period divided by units made
segments.shown_as: the list slides into a two-column table that pairs each factor with what it is paid (entrepreneur-profit, land-rent, labour-wages, capital-interest); arrows draw from the payments to 20K, 20K, 20K and 40K, a line sums them to 100K = 1,00,000; 'number of laptops = 10' writes above and a pink tag '1 laptop 10K' lands on the laptop box
segments.example: rent 20K + wages 20K + interest 20K + profit 40K = 100K per month; 10 laptops, so 10K each

segments.teaches: the laptop's factor cost is 10,000; the shop's factor cost (rent, electricity, maintenance, salaries) is 5,000; so GDP at factor cost is 15,000; market price = factor cost + indirect taxes - subsidies, which gives GDP at market price

elements.what: the framed taxed sale returns (10K, 2K tax, +5K, 1K tax, 15K struck to 18K) with GDP → Factor Cost / Market Price
red frame flashes on the laptop's 10K, then on the shop's +5K
'15K' fading in under Factor Cost
'= Factor Cost + Indirect Taxes - Subsidies' under Market Price
yellow underline under 'Indirect Taxes'

segments.notes: 5 change events in 53 s. Subsidies appear only in the formula; the example never has one. The shop's 'factor cost' list includes electricity and maintenance (doubtful as factor payments).
segments.idea: GDP at factor cost adds up what factors earn; market price adds indirect taxes and removes subsidies
segments.shown_as: the framed sale returns with the two GDP branches; a red frame flashes on the laptop's 10K, then on the shop's +5K, and '15K' fades in under Factor Cost; under Market Price the formula '= factor cost + indirect taxes - subsidies' writes on and 'indirect taxes' gets a yellow underline
segments.example: 10K + 5K = 15K at factor cost; 18K at market price

segments.teaches: three years with the same single laptop and service: factor cost stays 15,000, but the government raises indirect taxes so market price goes 18,000 → 20,000 → 25,000; GDP at market price rises with no extra production

elements.what: rows Year 2020, 2021, 2022 under the GDP branches; columns factor cost and market price
15K, 15K, 15K in the factor cost column
18K, 20K, 25K in the market price column
black up-arrow over 'indirect taxes' that grows taller with each rise

segments.notes: 4 detected events; the values write on with their spoken numbers (kf 289.7-339.7). 'Year 2020' is on screen but never said; the narrator speaks only of 2021 and 2022.
segments.idea: if only taxes rise, GDP at market price climbs while real production is flat
segments.shown_as: the frame drops away and the GDP branches move up over a three-row year table; 15K writes into the factor cost column for every year, while 18K, 20K and 25K write into the market price column and an up-arrow over 'indirect taxes' grows taller at each rise
segments.example: factor cost 15K each year; market price 18K (2020), 20K (2021), 25K (2022)

segments.teaches: GDP at factor cost is the better indicator of whether production is rising; India used it, but in 2015 switched to GDP at market price; the viewer is asked why (answer promised next video)

elements.what: question card at top left with a big '?': which is the better indicator of production?
hand reaching out from the card, pointing at Factor Cost, which gets a green box
green box moves to Market Price
white box: in 2015 India switched to GDP at market price
cluster of coloured question marks over the callout (comment prompt)

segments.notes: 6 change events in 41 s. The green box reaches Market Price about 3 s before 'market price' is said, while the voice still says India used factor cost.
segments.idea: to track production, use GDP at factor cost; India's headline moved to market price in 2015
segments.shown_as: a question card with a big '?' slides in at top left; a hand reaches out from it and points at Factor Cost, which lights in a green box; then the green box moves to Market Price, a callout says India switched to market price in 2015, and coloured question marks pop above it as the viewer is asked why
